title: Observed wind generation source
description: One publisher's dataset of observed (metered or reported) wind power output. Modelled or simulated output does not belong here.

id.description: Stable identifier: lower-case country or area code, then a short slug. Matches the file name.

name.description: The dataset's own name, in English where one exists.

publisher_role.description: What kind of body the publisher is.

countries.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes covered. Use the area field for a sub-national or multi-country market area.

area.description: Sub-national or market area, where narrower or wider than whole countries (for example 'NEM: QLD, NSW, VIC, SA, TAS').

level.description: Finest unit the output is reported for.

technology.description: Which fleets the series covers, and whether they are split.

measure.description: What the number actually is. Metered at the connection point, reported by the operator, estimated by the system operator, or a capacity factor.

end.description: Last year with data. Omit if the series is still updated.

update.description: How often new data appear (for example 'near real time', 'monthly', 'annual').

capacity.description: Whether an installed-capacity denominator comes with the series, so a capacity factor can be formed.

coordinates.description: Whether the publisher gives locations for the reported units.

curtailment.description: Whether curtailed or constrained-off output is reported, so available output can be reconstructed.

conventions.description: How to read the time stamps and the numbers. The commonest silent errors when joining generation to weather data are a wrong time zone, an end-of-period stamp read as a start, and power read as energy.

timezone.description: Zone of the published time stamps: 'UTC', an IANA zone that follows daylight saving ('Europe/Madrid'), a fixed offset all year ('UTC+01:00'), 'not-applicable' for monthly or annual data labelled by period, or 'unknown'.

timestamp.description: What a time stamp marks: the start of its period, the end of it, an instant (a snapshot reading), a label for a whole day, month or year, or unknown.

unit.description: Unit of the wind values as published, or unknown when the publisher does not state it.

value.description: What each value is over its period: a mean power, a total energy, an instantaneous reading, or unknown.

evidence.description: The publisher's page, file header or documentation that states the conventions.

note.description: Anything else, such as a daylight-saving quirk or a unit change between years.

key_required.description: A key or token is needed (usually free).

registration.description: An account is needed even to download.

languages.description: Languages the documentation is offered in (ISO 639-1).

name.description: Licence as the publisher names it.

spdx.description: SPDX identifier where one fits exactly.

url.description: Page the licence was read from.

redistribution.description: Whether the raw series may be re-hosted. 'unclear' means no reuse terms could be found or read.

attribution.description: Attribution text the publisher asks for.

verified.description: true only if the terms were read on the publisher's own page on last_checked.

traps.description: Known problems a user would otherwise find the hard way. Each needs evidence.

evidence.description: Link to a document, issue, commit or audit that shows the problem.

found.description: Date the trap was found or confirmed.

evidence_is_error.description: The evidence link is meant to fail: the error it returns (a 404 for a missing year, a validation message) is what shows the trap. The link checker then expects an error.

tools.description: Open-source clients that read this source.

last_checked.description: Date the entry was last checked against the source.

reviewed.description: false when the entry was compiled by an automated research pass and no person has yet checked it against the source. Omit once a person has.
